title: Input Bit Language Is Logarithmic-Space Decidable
statement: The language of binary strings of the form $\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle$, where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the encoding that doubles each bit of the first string and then appends $01$ and the second string, and where the zero-indexed bit $x_i$ exists and equals $1$, is decidable by a finite-state-set Turing machine using at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)$ work-tape cells on inputs of length $n$, for some natural number constant $c$.
